articleTitle: Design of a Portable Heart Rate and Temperature Monitoring System for the Elderly
abstract: This study introduces a portable heart rate and temperature monitoring system based on the STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller, designed to address the rising health concerns of the elderly. It tracks key physiological indicators, including heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen levels, using the MAX30100 sensor for non-invasive monitoring and the DS18B20 for precise temperature detection. The system provides real-time data via an LCD display and mobile app, with an alarm feature that activates when readings exceed predefined thresholds. The integration of the ESP8266 Wi-Fi module allows seamless data transmission to smartphones and cloud platforms, enabling remote access and management. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of system, offering a practical tool for improving elderly health care through early detection and proactive monitoring.

articleTitle: Constructing a Shopping Mall Customer Service Center Robot Based on the LLAMA-7B Language Model
abstract: This study develops a customer service robot powered by a large language model, deployed at Tainan Spinning Mall. The system runs on the Temi robot and leverages Llama3 fine-tuned using PEFT methods like LoRA to optimize performance on an NVIDIA L4 GPU with limited memory. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances response accuracy, while training data includes mall-specific datasets, such as store directories, product listings, and promotions, alongside general dialogue data. After model adaptation, it achieves 95% accuracy in answering mall-related inquiries, responding within five seconds, ensuring efficient and accurate assistance in fast-paced retail environments.

articleTitle: Research on Digital Marketing Strategies of Apparel Brands Based on Sustainable Consumption Behavior Among Youth Consumers
abstract: The rapid development of the apparel industry has resulted in a waste of resources and environmental damage. In this paper, under the background of "dual-carbon" policies, we take the youth population in Shanghai as an example to explore the characteristics of sustainable clothing consumption behavior. Through lifestyle segmentation, we classified the investigators among Shanghai youth group into four types of consumers and discover the characteristics of each group, so as to find effective ways to promote their sustainable clothing consumption. These four groups have significant differences in six aspects such as consumption tendency, disposal intention, used clothing recycling, and premium behavior. Finally, we put forward relevant digital marketing suggestions for apparel enterprises and help sustainable clothing brands to attract more young consumers.

articleTitle: 3D Visualization of Indoor Thermal Environment with UE5
abstract: This study focuses on the development of an advanced indoor thermal environment visualization system utilizing UE5, leveraging various blueprint features such as character blueprints and widget blueprints to implement interactive functionalities and dynamic simulations. The system effectively simulates indoor and outdoor heat transfer processes, allowing users to visualize and analyze key parameters of building facades with high accuracy. By providing intuitive thermal environment data, it aids in informed decision-making for architectural designs. Future work will focus on enhancing thermal calculation accuracy, streamlining data import workflows, and improving interactivity to create a more robust and user-friendly system for advanced thermal simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-Leaf Collimator Status Monitoring Based on Geometric Constraint of Strip Type Detector
abstract: This study presents an algorithm for multi-Leaf collimator status using photon signals acquired from a strip type detector. The multi-leaf collimator is rotated from 0 to 180 degrees in 10-degree increments, and at each angle, photon signals are captured and digitized using an analog-to-digital converter. The data is processed with a filtered back projection technique combined with two categories masks to improve and verify the reconstruction accuracy. A preliminary result shows the algorithm offering a reliable solution for verifying multi-leaf collimator configurations in radiation therapy. Meanwhile, the mask type will affect the reconstructed images and we found that the strip type detector could effectively detect and reconstruct the photon signals as well.

articleTitle: A study on the study motivation, study attitude and study satisfaction of students majoring in tourism in applied universities for professional certificate
abstract: This study aims to investigate the influence of learning motivation, learning attitude and learning satisfaction on the process of obtaining 1+X professional certificate for tourism majors in applied universities. The quantitative study tested students at three applied universities in Shanghai using an online questionnaire. A total of 658 questionnaires were distributed and 582 valid questionnaires were recovered. The questionnaire response rate was 88%. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis were used for data processing. The results of this study show that: 1. Teaching hardware facilities are the most satisfied with students' learning. 2. The item with the highest score for learning attitude is curriculum design. 3. There are significant differences in students' learning motivation, learning attitude and learning satisfaction under different background variables. 4. Students' learning motivation, learning attitude and learning satisfaction are all positively correlated. 5. Students' learning attitude has a significant predictive effect on learning satisfaction.Learn about the impact of different learning-related factors experienced by students of tourism majors in applied universities through their personal participation in the professional certificate learning process. The results of the research can help schools in formulating 1+X professional certificate courses and teaching to enable students to study more in colleges and improve the certificate acquisition rate.

articleTitle: Business Analysis: From Tools to Application
abstract: Business analysis requires various tools, each with unique features. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of tools, algorithms, and application fields in business analysis, highlighting their importance in addressing the growing complexity and volume of business data. Finally, the application of large language models in business analysis is discussed.

articleTitle: Design an apple-picking robot based on recognition of YOLOv5
abstract: This article takes apples as an example to establish the stable grasping parameters of the flexible grasping hand picker. The number and distribution of fingers are meticulously planned, and the driving technology of common flexible robots is compared to propose the grasping method of the picker's fingers. In addition, advanced finite element methods are used to build a comprehensive mechanical model of the flexible fingers, and the SW finite element software is used. The gripper designed based on the soft actuator has enhanced grasp tolerance and flexibility, reducing the strict requirements on grasping force and positioning accuracy, thereby improving work efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on the Construction and Application of an Interactive Cloud-Based Courseware Platform
abstract: Traditional paper textbooks suffer from long production cycles, outdated content, limited formats, poor indexing, and inefficient retrieval. To address these issues, we propose a cloud-based platform that leverages cloud computing to create interactive courseware with custom code execution capabilities. The platform integrates functions for writing, converting, deploying, presenting, and interacting with code, enhancing textbook creation and utilization. Initial teaching applications show significant improvements in teaching quality, support for continuous learning, and overall better educational outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancing Stored Grain Pest Detection with Improved YOLOv8-BiFPN Model
abstract: Grain pests in storage present a major risk to the world’s food safety. The research delves into a multi-scale pest identification technique utilizing machine vision and introduces an enhanced YOLOv8-BiFPN model. Utilizing the GrainPest dataset comprising 500 images of diverse grains and pests, the YOLOv8-BiFPN demonstrated superior performance compared to the baseline model. With random dataset partitioning, YOLOv8-BiFPN achieved a 94.8% mAP, improving by 2.57% over the original. The study suggests that random partitioning is sufficiently effective without manual intervention. The improved YOLOv8-BiFPN shows promise in detecting pests against complex backgrounds and small targets, offering a more effective approach for pest management in storage. Future work will focus on enhancing classification accuracy and finding optimal dataset partitioning strategies.

articleTitle: YOLO Algorithm for Ripeness Detection in Greenhouse Cucumbers
abstract: Accurate identification and classification of crop maturity are essential for optimizing production efficiency in smart agriculture. This study improves cucumber maturity detection by optimizing the YOLO algorithm, focusing on YOLOv5 and YOLOv8, to address challenges in greenhouse environments. A dataset of over 3,000 labeled images across various growth stages, lighting conditions, and environmental factors was used to train and evaluate the models.The results show that YOLOv8n outperforms the other models, achieving 97% recall and 96% precision in high-confidence intervals, making it the most effective model for complex cucumber maturity detection. YOLOv5n, while slightly lower in performance, excelled in medium to low-confidence ranges, offering a good balance of speed and accuracy. YOLOv8n achieved an overall mAP of 0.469, while YOLOv5n reached 0.424, further highlighting YOLOv8n’s superior performance.This study also explored an ensemble approach combining YOLOv5n, YOLOv5x, and YOLOv8n, which led to improved recall and precision, addressing misclassification and low-confidence detections. These findings highlight the importance of model optimization and data diversity in cucumber maturity detection, suggesting that combined YOLO models provide significant advantages for smart agriculture applications.This research contributes to improving the automation and accuracy of crop maturity classification, offering insights for the future of agricultural automation and more efficient farming practices.

articleTitle: A Non-invasive AI Oral Health Monitoring System: A Solution for Elderly Oral Health in Remote Areas
abstract: As global populations age, oral health concerns have become a significant health issue, especially among the elderly and those in remote areas with limited access to healthcare resources. This study proposes a non-invasive oral health monitoring system integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and voice recognition technologies to assess key indicators, including tongue coating, dental plaque, oral motor function, and oral dryness. The system allows users to conduct self-assessments at home via mobile devices, offering real-time diagnosis and reducing barriers to oral health management in underserved communities. Initial experiments show the system demonstrates high accuracy and reliability in detecting oral health issues, validating the feasibility and effectiveness of non-invasive monitoring.

articleTitle: Assessing the Effectiveness of Easy-to-Read Principles in Different Generative AI Models: Enhancing Knowledge Acquisition for People with Disabilities
abstract: The principles of easy-to-read (E2R) materials are crucial for individuals with disabilities, as they simplify language, provide clear structures, and use user-friendly designs to reduce the difficulty in understanding information. These principles help individuals overcome barriers to comprehending important content. Online friendships have become a common form of social interaction in today's society; providing easy-to-understand online safety knowledge to people with disabilities has become an important issue in public health and social participation. However, existing educational resources are often insufficient, and developing materials that adhere to E2R principles requires significant time and resources. To address the challenge of insufficient resources, the study introduces generative AI technology to rapidly and effectively create educational materials that comply with E2R principles to meet the learning needs of individuals with disabilities regarding online friendship safety. This study examines the performance of three generative AI models—GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-sonnet, and Gemini-1.5-pro—in developing educational materials based on E2R principles, specifically tailored to provide appropriate online safety knowledge for individuals with disabilities. The research was conducted in two stages: the first stage evaluated the AI models' ability to generate basic knowledge.In contrast, the second stage assessed their ability to integrate E2R principles into generating educational materials. The evaluation used statistical methods, including the Wilcox-on and Kruskal-Wallis tests, to determine each AI model's outcomes in both stages. The results showed that GPT-4o performed best across both stages, consistently generating complete and coherent knowledge and materials. Claude-3.5-sonnet followed closely, with some fluctuations but overall stable performance. Gemini-1.5-pro performed the worst, producing unstable content with significant variability. The findings of this study are significant, as they indicate that GPT-4o is the most suitable AI model for developing easy-to-read educational materials, whether for basic knowledge generation or for integrating external E2R resources to create online friendship safety materials. This research provides empirical evidence and design recommendations that can guide the future use of AI technology in creating educational materials tailored to vulnerable groups.

articleTitle: A Novel E-commerce Recommendation System Based on RAG and Pretrained Large Model
abstract: The exponential growth of e-commerce platforms necessitates efficient and scalable recommendation systems to enhance user experience and business performance. This paper introduces a novel recommendation system based on the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework, leveraging customer review data as an external, modular knowledge source. Unlike traditional systems that require global computations over user-product matrices, the proposed system employs FAISS for efficient vector-based retrieval and BART for natural language generation, reducing computational overhead and enhancing scalability. The system is implemented as a web-based application offering two functionalities: checking if a specific product is recommended based on reviews and generating product recommendations from user queries. Evaluation demonstrates the system’s ability to provide accurate, user-friendly recommendations while maintaining extensibility and adaptability to dynamic datasets. This work establishes a foundation for modular, review-driven recommendation systems in real-world e-commerce scenarios.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in The Integration Of Education, Science And Practice
abstract: This article is the preliminary stage of data presentation about artificial intelligence, an upcoming issue today. What is artificial intelligence in the article? The importance of artificial intelligence in education, science, and integration is addressed. One of the hottest topics in the present world is artificial intelligence. How will the artificial intelligence revolution affect humanity in the future? Will it have a future raises open questions? We want to remind you of another aspect of the time on artificial intelligence touch through literature, education, science, and practice integration, and it will dwell upon the importance and role of artificial intelligence that we found opposite. The author(s) provide short information concerning the above topic before delving into the discussion of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Enhancing Adaptability and Efficiency in Industrial Robotics: A Study on Intelligent Pallet Stacking Systems
abstract: Robotic arms have been indispensable tools in industry, not only improving the efficiency of production workflows but also continuously performing highly repetitive and high-load tasks. For humans, such work could cause irreversible mental and physical harm. However, many manufacturers face the challenge of systems being unable to quickly adapt to streamline changes when implementing robotic arm systems. Each product adjustment requires trained personnel to adjust the equipment, leading to failures in robotic arm system implementation. Therefore, this study has designed a set of software control rules for pallet stacking processes. Robotic arms can quickly adjust according to these rules to adapt to different product stacking needs and automatically calculate the optimal stacking method. Furthermore, this study has also designed a user-friendly interface, making system configuration simpler and more convenient, ultimately aiming to allow users to work in a happy and elegant environment.

articleTitle: Personalized Audiobook Generation Using Voice Cloning and Text-to-Speech Synthesis
abstract: This project leverages advancements in voice cloning and text-to-speech (TTS) to develop a novel audio converter for personalized audiobook creation. Users upload a brief voice sample, allowing the system to learn and replicate unique vocal characteristics, such as tone and pitch, producing customized audio outputs. Integrating voice cloning with natural language processing (NLP) and TTS, the system first analyzes text to identify characters, dialogues, and emotional cues. This enables realistic, expressive narration tailored to each character and context. Unlike traditional TTS, this approach reduces monotony, allowing users to "narrate" stories in their own voice, creating an immersive and individualized listening experience.

articleTitle: Java Batik Classification Based on The Pattern Using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: The intricate art of batik holds profound cultural significance in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia, where it serves as a conduit for transmitting ancient narratives, philosophies, and rituals. This research endeavors to deepen our understanding of Javanese regional batik by employing machine-learning techniques for classification. Focused on the island of Java, renowned for the diversity and distinct identities of its batik patterns across different regions, this study aims to contribute to preserving and recognizing this rich cultural heritage.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Algorithm in Waste Classification using Real-Time Object Detection
abstract: Poor waste management can adversely impact the environment, hindering its optimal performance. Implementing advanced item detection methods offers a more innovative solution to waste management challenges. This study explores the use of image processing with YOLO (You Only Look Once) for trash detection. By leveraging deep learning technology, it classifies various types of waste objects. A reliable classification system facilitates faster and more accurate waste segregation. YOLOv5s, known for its fast real-time object detection capabilities, effectively identifies and categorizes different types of waste.

articleTitle: Crop Pest and Disease Recognition Based on Improved ConvNeXt and Swin Transformer
abstract: Agriculture is essential for global food security, which significantly impacts human happiness and overall wellbeing. As the population grows, improving agricultural productivity becomes crucial for ensuring a stable food supply and supporting societal welfare. Pests have long affected crop yields, threatening both food security and quality of life. This paper leverages deep learning by combining ConvNeXt and Swin Transformer models. A newly proposed attention mechanism, CAFM Fusion, enhances feature fusion, while Mixup and dynamic learning rate adjustment help prevent overfitting. Tested on IP102 and PlantVillage datasets, our model achieved 75.75% and 99.89% accuracy, respectively, contributing to sustainable agriculture and better well-being.

articleTitle: Feature Align-HFL: A Feature Alignment Based Client-Specific Model For Heterogeneous Federated Learning
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables decentralized model training while ensuring data privacy between clients and the server, and is applicable in various domains such as healthcare, finance, and edge computing. Traditional FL approaches assume homogeneous model architectures across clients and servers, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios where clients use diverse models. To address this, we introduce Feature Align-HFL, a novel framework designed for Heterogeneous Federated Learning (HFL) that aligns dissimilar models for effective knowledge sharing. Specifically, we demonstrate its application by aligning CNNs and U-Nets for a common classification task. By employing cosine similarity, Feature Align-HFL identifies and aligns common features across heterogeneous models. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset show that CNN and adapted U-Net models achieved 90 percent and 86 percent accuracy, respectively, with feature map similarities reaching up to 96 percent. These results highlight the significant transferable knowledge between dissimilar architectures, indicating that Feature Align-HFL can effectively support knowledge sharing in heterogeneous FL settings.

articleTitle: Crop Yield Prediction based on Attention-LSTM Model
abstract: With the widespread application of big data and artificial intelligence technologies in the agricultural sector, accurate prediction of crop yields has become crucial, not only for food security but also for significantly enhancing agricultural management efficiency. This paper delves into various prediction models, including traditional machine learning algorithms and deep learning-based time series prediction models, with a particular focus on the integration of the attention mechanism with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. By constructing an LSTM model fused with the attention mechanism (Attention Mechanism LSTM Model, Attention-LSTM), this study significantly improves the accuracy of crop yield predictions, which is of great significance for ensuring the stability of food supply and optimizing the allocation of agricultural resources.In the experimental section, a large dataset encompassing factors such as fertilizer usage and soil properties was used to rigorously test the Attention-LSTM model. The results showed that, compared to models such as BP neural networks, GRU, BILSTM, and LSTM, the Attention-LSTM exhibited excellent performance in key evaluation metrics including RMSE, MSE, and MAPE, achieving significant improvement in prediction accuracy and enhancement of generalization ability.The contribution of this paper lies in the development of the Attention-LSTM model, which, with its efficient and precise crop yield prediction capabilities, provides a powerful tool for enhancing the level of agricultural intelligence and optimizing agricultural production decisions. It also showcases the vast potential of deep learning technologies in smart agriculture.

articleTitle: Design of Instant Communication Blind Cane Based on STM32
abstract: This paper aims to address the severe travel challenges faced by people with visual impairments. The research introduces an innovative system that ingeniously combines cane hardware with Internet of Things (IoT) technology. At the core of this system is the STM32F103C6T6 microcontroller, which is seamlessly integrated with an OLED display to provide clear visual feedback. A voice broadcast controller offers auditory navigation, while multiple sensors are used to detect the surrounding environment. Communication modules enable uninterrupted interaction. Key hardware modules, including the JQ6500 voice module, gyroscope posture detection module, ultrasonic control module, GSM SMS sending module, and buzzer module, work in harmony to provide comprehensive functionality. The software design includes in-depth analyses of the main program and individual module programs. Rigorous experimental testing has demonstrated the remarkable stability and accuracy of the system in obstacle detection and positioning. Looking to the future, subsequent research will focus on integrating voice recognition technology. This will not only enhance the functionality of the system but also provide better services for people with visual impairments, enabling them to explore their surroundings with greater confidence and independence.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv5 Model for Real-Time Fish Species Recognition on Jetson Orin Nano
abstract: This study develops a real-time fish recognition model using eYOLOv5, implemented on Jetson Orin Nano for an interactive display system. Tailored for fish identification, it displays results and 3D images instantly, supported by a database of 50 underwater species, addressing limited guides in marine parks. The Jetson Orin Nano ensures portability and efficiency as an embedded platform. The eYOLOv5 model, based on a CNN, incorporates adaptive activation functions and attention mechanisms, achieving 97% accuracy after training on 10,000 labeled images. It enhances recognition accuracy and user experience, showcasing deep learning potential in underwater identification. Jetson Orin Nano’s high performance, low power use, and compact size enable real-time processing without cloud reliance, reducing latency and boosting stability, portability, and flexibility. This system suits marine exhibitions and education, delivering seamless recognition.

articleTitle: Prediction of Stock Prices Using a Combination of LSTM and GRU Algorithms on LQ45 Indexed Stocks
abstract: Stock investment is a popular choice due to its high profit potential, but stock price movements influenced by various factors make predictions challenging. This study combines LSTM and GRU algorithms in an LSTM-GRU-LSTM-GRU configuration to predict the stock prices of five companies from the LQ45 index (ADRO, ANTM, ESSA, PGAS, PTBA) using daily closing prices and transaction volumes. The model’s performance was evaluated using different dataset splits (70:30, 80:20, 90:10) and epoch parameters (10, 20, 30, 40, 50), measured using RMSE and MAPE metrics. The results show that combining LSTM and GRU models provides reasonably accurate predictions with specific dataset compositions and epoch settings. For ADRO, the best combination was 90:10 with 30 epochs (RMSE 0.0183, MAPE 2.3619%); for ANTM, 90:10 with 30 epochs (RMSE 0.0110, MAPE 1.5968%); for ESSA, 80:20 with 40 epochs (RMSE 0.0103, MAPE 3.7750%); for PGAS, 90:10 with 40 epochs (RMSE 0.0046, MAPE 2.5603%); and for PTBA, 70:30 with 50 epochs (RMSE 0.0066, MAPE 2.7489%). The model shows a good ability to capture stock price trends, despite some significant deviations, particularly in PTBA and ADRO stocks. These findings affirm that the combination of LSTM and GRU can enhance stock price prediction accuracy, with further improvements possible through model parameter adjustments to reduce deviations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of BERT and Traditional Machine Learning Models in E-commerce Review Classification
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of sentiment classification methods applied to a dataset of Amazon reviews. Three methods are evaluated: the pre-trained BERT model, Naive Bayes with TF-IDF, and the lexicon-based TextBlob. The dataset consists of 20,350 samples, with 5,869 positive and 14,481 negative reviews, derived by categorizing ratings of 4 and 5 as positive, and 1 and 2 as negative. Results show that Naive Bayes achieved the highest accuracy (86.62%), excelling in negative sentiment classification, while BERT demonstrated a balanced performance with 84.81% accuracy and superior contextual understanding. TextBlob, with an accuracy of 69.79%, struggled to classify positive sentiments due to its reliance on predefined lexicons. The study highlights the strengths and trade-offs of each method, emphasizing BERT’s potential for achieving state-of-the-art results in sentiment analysis, albeit with higher computational costs.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enhanced Heart Rate Prediction: Comparing Machine Learning and Time Series Approaches in MIoT
abstract: This research investigates the preservation of heart rate data in Medical IoT (MIoT) systems using blockchain technology. The study evaluates several machine learning and time series models, including Decision Tree Regressor, Neural Network, LSTM, and ARIMA. The study compares these models’ prediction performance and ability to maintain data integrity in a blockchain-secured environment. The evaluation metric performance indicates towards Decision Tree Regressor (DTR) and Neural Network (NN) models which outperform in forcasting heart rate data with minimum MSE, MAE and more viable R2 and Explained Variance scores. These outcomes suggest great accuracy and reliability.In contrast, the LSTM and ARIMA models perform inadequately, displaying substantial error metrics and negative scores, highlighting that they are unsuited for this particular prediction job. Overall, the Decision Tree Regressor and Neural Network models are the most successful in forecasting heart rate in this study.

articleTitle: Fall Detection Algorithm for Elderly People Living Alone Based on ARKit and YOLOv5
abstract: The article presents a fall detection algorithm for elderly people living alone based on ARKit and YOLOv5. By combining ARKit’s spatial perception capabilities with YOLOv5’s high-speed visual analysis, the algorithm can quickly and accurately identify elderly people falling. It comprises functional modules such as data collection and fall detection. It adopts the operating environment of the iOS platform and is developed using Swift, Object-C++, and Python languages. The algorithm demonstrates strong fall detection performance with high accuracy, recall, and mAP. However, limitations in the versions of YOLO as well as the size and diversity of the dataset. Future work could focus on using different YOLO versions, expanding the dataset, changing the network structure, and introducing more techniques to improve the accuracy and performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Bottlenecks and improvement strategies for digital transformation in manufacturing
abstract: This paper explores the main bottlenecks faced by the manufacturing industry in the process of digital transformation as well as improving strategies. The bottlenecks include inventory management problems, insufficient work standardization, lack of visual management, error-proofing devices, and safety protection measures that small and medium-sized enterprises often face. This study proposes short-term, medium-term, and long-term improvement strategies. This article demonstrates the implementation effects of various improvement strategies by introducing the practical case of Company Y, collecting and organizing on-site data, and then analyzing value stream mapping. At the same time, it also proposes suggestions for future research.

articleTitle: Short - term Load Forecasting Method for Distinguishing Building Types in the Heating System
abstract: First, the heat usage characteristics of different building types in the heating system were analyzed. Then, a correlation analysis was conducted on quantifiable factors that may affect the demand-side load, and the top five factors with the highest correlation coefficients were selected as input features for the load forecasting model. A Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm, optimized using Grid Search (GS) and Cross-Validation (CV), was used to construct the forecasting models. This resulted in separate load forecasting models for public buildings, residential buildings, and a mixed model. These models were then used to predict the hourly load demand for the next 12 hours at the heat stations. The results show that constructing separate forecasting models for different building types improves the short-term load forecasting capability and enhances the prediction accuracy. This provides reliable load forecasts for predictive control in the heating system, reducing energy waste due to over-supply and improving user comfort by avoiding under-supply

articleTitle: Key Factor Analysis of Computer Applications and Technologies Curriculum Based on Professional Certificate Program in Higher Vocational Education
abstract: With the advancement of professional certification in higher vocational education, the formulation of talent training programs has become particularly important. Taking the Computer Application Technology major at Changzhou College of Information Technology as a case study, this paper explores several key elements in writing talent training programs under the background of professional certification: career orientation, training objectives, and graduation requirements. Firstly, it analyzes the sources of content in the career orientation table, especially the focus on main positions. Secondly, it clarifies the method for setting training objectives, providing a general template and an example for the Computer Application Technology major. Finally, it elaborates on the formulation of graduation requirements, particularly the decomposition of indicators to ensure they sufficiently support the graduation requirements. The research aims to provide references and insights for higher vocational colleges to optimize their talent training programs in the context of professional certification.

articleTitle: Motion Data Collection for Dance Movements based on Inertial Sensors
abstract: Dance requires professional instruction during the learning and training process, but high-level guidance at any time and any place can be a challenge. In the context of Orange Technology oriented towards human well-being and health care, this paper proposes fixing the data acquisition device terminals on different parts of the body of dancers, motion data during dance performances can be automatically collected. This data is sent to the server side for processing and then stored in the database, and the nine-axis dynamic data collected from various body parts is displayed on the Web page of the user side in time. By reviewing this data, dancers can be guided to improve their pose, helping them enhance their professional skills and experience a sense of satisfaction and happiness during the dance.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Virtual Nursing Systems: Revolutionizing Patient Education in Modern Healthcare
abstract: Traditional patient education relies on static brochures, lacking interactivity and increasing healthcare providers' workload. This study introduces a virtual nurse dialogue system using ASR and a fine-tuned LLama3 8B LLM trained on Traditional Chinese medical texts. A RAG framework with a structured knowledge base enhances accuracy and minimizes misinformation. The system features an RWD-based interface with 3D animations and synchronized voice outputs for an immersive experience. Experimental results show 95% accuracy and responses under 5 seconds, with 90% user satisfaction, demonstrating its potential to enhance patient education and reduce healthcare burdens.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Student Comprehensive Assessment System
abstract: With the continuous deepening of educational informatization, student comprehensive assessment has become increasingly important as a core link in evaluating academic achievements and promoting the improvement of teaching quality. However, some schools still lack sufficient educational informatization and rely on Excel spreadsheets to analyze students comprehensive assessment data, resulting in low work efficiency. This paper proposes a student comprehensive assessment system based on the Django framework, which deeply investigates the functional requirements of existing student comprehensive assessments and designs corresponding functional modules such as honor declaration, moral education evaluation, academic performance inquiry, dormitory performance accounting, and comprehensive performance inquiry. Based on the different weights of the entered data, the system can quickly calculate the comprehensive assessment scores for each student. The system also integrates a large language model from Qianfan, developing an intelligent question assistant to deeply learn the school's policy knowledge base to answer questions encountered by teachers and students in their learning and daily lives. The deployment and implementation of the system have verified the accuracy of the student comprehensive assessment results, improved the level of educational informatization management in student work, and promoted the development of the student comprehensive assessment system.

articleTitle: New Efficient Depth Estimation and Real-Time Object 3D Recognition Models for Humanoid Robotic Environment Understanding
abstract: As demand for 3D visual capabilities in humanoid robots increases, the limitations of traditional methods are becoming evident. Point-cloud techniques, while effective for 3D reconstruction, are hindered by computational complexity and extensive data collection. Conversely, monocular depth estimation networks (mono-Net) are simpler but only suitable for specific VR applications, struggling to accurately measure real-world 3D coordinates. Both approaches can be slow for real-time use. To overcome this, we developed an efficient multi-object 3D detection system using coordinate mapping and object-scale aware median filtering. Our simulations show that this system outperforms existing methods, achieving over 90% accuracy and a 0.066-second inference time on an RTX-3060 GPU laptop, making it ideal for visual Edge-AI applications in logistic robots and cruise robots.

articleTitle: Deep learning system for abdominal disease detection and localization
abstract: CT images are usually grayscale images and contain a large amount of medical information. However, deep learning research is still relatively insufficient for automatically detecting and segmenting lesions in abdominal CT images. This is due to the complexity of abdominal organs and their variability among different patients, which poses a high challenge to the algorithm. Using the improved Unet model combined with the transfer learning method for abdominal CT image segmentation can significantly improve the detection and diagnosis accuracy of liver tumors, kidney tumors, appendicitis, and other lesions. The Unet model was originally designed for the segmentation of biomedical images. It has end-to-end learning capabilities and can perform fine segmentation at the pixel level. The improved Unet model has made some important improvements based on the original structure, including adding data preprocessing and attention mechanisms, thereby improving the model’s segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. The transfer learning method uses a pre-trained model on a large data set and then applies it to the task of abdominal CT image segmentation. To validate our proposed approach, we conducted rigorous testing on a dedicated dataset. We evaluated key metrics such as accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, and DICE coefficient to evaluate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Skill-Driven Loan Prediction for Economic Inclusion: A Computational Approach for Financial Empowerment
abstract: In this paper, we propose an innovative loan prediction framework by developing an Adaptive random forest ensemble (ARFE) model, that integrates financial metrics with skill-based insights derived from the GEMMA large language model (LLM). Traditional credit evaluation models often overlook applicants’ skills, potentially excluding capable individuals with limited financial histories. The proposed ARFE model adapts to both financial and skill attributes, leveraging GEMMA’s fine-tuned skill ratings to enhance prediction accuracy and inclusivity. By emphasizing applicants’ human skill, ARFE offers a more equitable approach to loan evaluation, particularly benefiting underrepresented individuals in resource-limited regions. Comparative analysis with other baseline models demonstrates ARFE’s superior performance across accuracy, precision, and recall metrics, thus underscoring the potential of skill-inclusive models to redefine credit assessment, promoting fairer financial access and addressing systemic biases in traditional lending.

articleTitle: Research on Short Video Marketing of China Tourist Resorts Based on Web Text Analysis
abstract: For China tourist resorts, short videos have become a fast way to attract the attention of potential users. User’s comments on the short video platforms directly reflect attitudes toward the tourist destination. The comments are analyzed by using ROST CM6 and ROST EA to identify high-frequency words, semantic networks, and emotional tendencies. The authors identify five key factors of short video marketing and subsequently construct a model for applying short video marketing in the context of China tourism marketing. The model is used as a basis for the formulation of recommendations for short tourism video marketing strategies, which are designed to address identified deficiencies and enhance the efficacy of short video marketing. Finally, the authors put forward five recommendations for short tourism video marketing.

articleTitle: Improving Accuracy of Object Quantity and Text-Image Alignment Based on the Stable Diffusion Pretrained Model
abstract: In recent years, advancements in training methods using large-scale text-image datasets and the development of diffusion models have significantly improved the quality and efficiency of image generation from text prompts. Despite these strides, text-to-image generation models still face challenges in producing realistic images that accurately reflect the specified details in the prompts. A common issue with diffusion-based models is their difficulty in generating the precise number of objects described in the text. For instance, a prompt like "six tomatoes in a basket" may often result in an image with an incorrect number of tomatoes. To address this problem, this paper proposes an algorithm designed to enhance the accuracy of object quantity in generated images. The algorithm employs an object counting network to assess the number of objects in a given image and calculates the error between this predicted count and the expected count. This error gradient is then used to guide the predictions of the diffusion model, improving its ability to generate the specified number of objects accurately.

articleTitle: Intelligent Electrostatic Oil Fume Treatment Method Utilizing IoT Technology
abstract: Electrostatic precipitators are widely recognized as effective air pollution control equipment by environmental protection agencies. These devices utilize high voltage to generate an electrostatic field, causing oil fumes and dust particles to polarize. Through electrostatic attraction, these particles are captured on collector plates, achieving high-efficiency filtration. However, traditional electrostatic precipitators require frequent cleaning and maintenance, leading to operational downtime and increased costs. This study proposes a novel solution: integrating IoT technologies into electrostatic precipitators to create a smart system capable of real-time monitoring and data analysis. Sensors embedded in the system collect data such as sparking frequency, voltage, current, temperature, and air pressure. By leveraging big data analytics, maintenance can be optimized, reducing costs and human effort. This innovation holds significant value for the restaurant industry, ensuring compliance with air pollution laws while improving operational efficiency. Furthermore, this research aligns with global sustainability initiatives, including the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), by advancing eco-friendly technology and addressing critical environmental challenges.

articleTitle: Research of Applying Artificial Intelligence to Vocational Education: Personalized Exploration about Career Planning and Training
abstract: The traditional teaching and career planning models in vocational colleges struggle to meet students’ personalized needs, leading to inefficient resource allocation, limited individualized teaching, and a lack of dynamic adjustment mechanisms. Restrictions in course selection and mismatches between students and courses further hinder their potential development. This paper examines the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in vocational education, proposing a personalized framework for career planning and skills training. This research highlights AI’s role in course optimization, career pathways, elective customization, and employment feedback, presenting a model to improve teaching quality and support the digital transformation of vocational colleges.

articleTitle: Real-time System of Student Attendance Based on YOLO
abstract: Student attendance is a part of the regular academic performance of some college students, and attendance rate is also an important indicator for evaluating teaching quality. The commonly used traditional methods such as roll call, swiping student cards, distance check-in, and gesture check-in all have some problems, such as low efficiency, student attendance fraud, inability to keep real-time statistics, and students leaving after attendance. Real time and accurate calculation of student attendance has become an urgent demand for some universities and teachers. In recent years, models such as face detection and recognition in object detection have been widely used in scenarios such as liveness detection, crowd counting, and security authentication. This article will design and implement a real-time student attendance counting system, using the popular face detection algorithm YOLO as the core technology, aiming to solve the problems encountered by the current attendance system mentioned above.

articleTitle: Natural-Prosodic Cross-Lingual Personalized TTS
abstract: Despite long-standing efforts in speech synthesis technology, several shortcomings persist, including unnatural pronunciation, rigid cross-lingual synthesis, the presence of synthesized noise artifacts, and inadequate synthesis speed. Customizing a speech synthesis system to accurately mimic the timbre, intonation, rhythm, and prosody of specific speakers remains a significant challenge. To address these deficiencies, we present an advanced text-to-speech (TTS) AI model that seamlessly integrates autoregressive modeling, BERT, HuBERT, and self-supervised learning within the VITS framework. This model, referred to as ABS-VITS, enhances VITS by enabling high-fidelity synthesis that more realistically mimics human speech. The BERT component effectively extracts features necessary for reconstructing vocal timbre, while randomized duration prediction generates speech with diverse linguistic rhythms—critical elements for simulating human pronunciation. By strategically organizing and applying these pretrained models, ABS-VITS achieves a high degree of accuracy in producing speech waveforms from text inputs. Notably, the proposed network framework allows users to select their desired target speaker, significantly enhancing the naturalness of the synthesized speech after rapid fine-tuning. Consequently, this model facilitates personalized cross-lingual speech synthesis that emulates vivid prosodic emotions.

articleTitle: Flame Detection using YOLOv5 with K-means Optimized Anchor Boxes
abstract: Object detection is a challenging task in the domain of computer vision, aiming to identify and localize objects within images or videos. However, there are still research gaps in enhancing detection accuracy and processing speed, especially in complex backgrounds and with various object scales. In this study, we adopt an improved YOLOv5 model incorporating K-means clustering to optimize the anchor boxes, aiming to enhance flame detection performance. The proposed approach features the integration of K-means for better anchor box initialization, which enables more accurate bounding box predictions. Through comparative experiments on a self-constructed dataset, the results demonstrate that the K-means optimization strategy effectively improves the detection capability of YOLOv5. The accuracy of the proposed model increased from 86.91% to 88.29%, confirming the effectiveness of the optimization.

articleTitle: Research on Construction and Retrieval Mechanism for Cross Domain Engineering Archives Based on Knowledge Graph
abstract: With the development of social economy and the increase of engineering construction projects, a large number of engineering archives of various industries have been constructed. Archives are often scattered across different units and institutions, making it difficult to achieve centralized management and sharing of archives, resulting in prominent problems such as missing and errors while retrieving cross domain engineering archives. Therefore, we propose the Construction and Retrieval Mechanism for Cross Domain Engineering Archives Based on Knowledge Graph (CRM4CDA) for improving retrieval performance. In order to construct a visual knowledge graph for cross domain engineering archives, we combine Protégé tools with Neo4j graph database and integrate fragmented data to build ontology and extract entities for achieving knowledge fusion and integration. In order to improve retrieval performance, we employ semantic analysis, intelligent retrieval, and inference to improve retrieval efficiency. Knowledge association technology and transfer methods are also utilized to promote cross domain retrieval performance. At the same time, various measures are taken to ensure the privacy protection for archive retrieval. Both theoretical analysis and practice have shown that our CRM4CDA mechanism has the characteristics of high retrieval accuracy, recall rate, and efficiency. Further research will be carried out for exploring the deep integration of artificial intelligence and knowledge graphs to further improve the intelligence level of archive management.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Of Deep Learning Architectures For The Classification Of Eye-Related Diseases
abstract: Eye-related disorders are among the driving causes of vision impedances worldwide. Accurate classification of retinal conditions is crucial for adequate treatment and management. This research explores the potential of three advanced deep-learning models, namely—-VGG16, DenseNet, and Swin Transformers, to classify four eye-related disorders utilizing the Optical Coherence Tomography Image Retinal Database (OCTID) taken from ICPSR. The OCTID dataset contains retinal OCT images representing four distinct pathological conditions: age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, central serous retinopathy, macular holes, and normal retinas. Evaluation is done based on metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The comparison of these models, paired with interpretability techniques such as GRADCAM and Integrated Gradients, reveals that VGG16 achieves the highest F1-score, demonstrating robust classification performance. At the same time, Swin Transformers develops competitive accuracy with practical interpretability through Integrated Gradients. DenseNet showed slightly lower metrics but performed adequately on the GRADCAM outputs. This study underscores the critical role of advanced deep learning frames, which work to enhance diagnostic accuracy for retinal disorders and provide a foundation for future developments in ophthalmic disease classification.

articleTitle: Intelligent IoT Platform for Real-Time Monitoring of Indoor Air Quality in Healthcare Facilities
abstract: In recent years, people have been confronted with unprecedented emerging infectious diseases. Medical institutions typically manage high-risk infectious diseases, which are transmitted via droplets or airborne routes, by using negative pressure isolation rooms to house patients and provide medical care. These isolation areas and rooms are specially designed to effectively prevent the spread of pathogens, with the goal of protecting healthcare personnel and preventing large-scale hospital-acquired infections.As most medical institutions have already completed the installation of hardware, wired network construction is not ideal for hospital environments, as it would require modifications to existing infrastructure, indirectly affecting the quality of the hospital environment, such as noise from construction and the layout of piping systems. Therefore, this study proposes an "Intelligent IoT Platform for Real-Time Monitoring of Indoor Air Quality in Healthcare Institutions." The system leverages smart sensors integrated with the Internet of Things (IoT), utilizing the small size and ease of deployment of the sensors as part of the overall technical framework. The platform also incorporates health and safety indicators relevant to hospital hygiene, enabling the monitoring of various environmental factors to ensure the safety of healthcare personnel.

articleTitle: Comparison of Naïve Bayes Classifier Algorithm and Support Vector Machine Classification for the Sport Event at X Platform
abstract: The Indonesian U-23 national team managed to qualify for the semifinals in the AFC U-23 event in Qatar even though they failed to win first place against Uzbekistan and third place against Iraq. On social media Twitter (x), Indonesia’s match at AFC U-23 as a new debutant became a hot topic of conversation among Indonesian netizens. Various groups of people support it through their opinions. Several opinions from the public on Twitter (X) will be used as research data for sentiment analysis regarding the AFC U-23 event. This research uses the Naïve Bayes Classifier and Support Vector Machine (SVM) methods which are expected to have a good level of accuracy. Based on the research results, it was found that different levels of accuracy from several data set divisions were divided into 3 (three) types, namely 80:20, 90:10 and 75:25. The use of the Naïve Bayes method produced a higher level of accuracy than the Support Vector method. Machine (SVM) with accuracy results in the data (80:20) for Naïve Bayes achieved an accuracy of 97.83% while for the Support Vector Machine it achieved an accuracy of 97.29%. For the data (90:10) the Naïve Bayes method reached 96.77% while for the Support Vector Machine it was 95.69% and for the data (75:25) the Naïve Bayes method got an accuracy value of 97.83% and the Support Vector Machine accuracy value was 97.83% and produced sentiment. analysis is classified as positive.

articleTitle: Toward Indonesia Cement Decarbonization: A Survey on Machine Learning Model
abstract: Climate change and global warming present significant global challenges, urging industries to embrace sustainable practices. In Indonesia, the cement industry is a major contributor to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, accounting for 4% of global CO2 emissions. This paper outlines a decarbonization roadmap for Indonesia's cement sector, targeting net-zero emissions (NZE) by 2050. Key approaches include lowering the clinker factor, using alternative fuels, improving energy efficiency, and implementing advanced technologies such as Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS). An ensemble learning model is introduced to forecast GHG emission reduction scenarios and optimize mitigation strategies. By harnessing artificial intelligence, the model provides precise predictions and actionable recommendations to effectively curb emissions. The research highlights Indonesia’s dedication to global climate commitments, emphasizing the cement industry's vital role in achieving the country’s Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (ENDC) goals. This ongoing study establishes a framework for integrating cutting-edge machine learning techniques into decarbonization initiatives, supporting sustainable development in Indonesia's cement industry.

articleTitle: Research on 1+2N Architecture of Distributed Archive Warehouse for Construction and Sharing
abstract: Engineering archives are important materials generated during the construction, operation, and maintenance processes of engineering projects. Due to the involvement of various technologies and industries in actual engineering projects, there are corresponding new demands for regional digital archive information sharing, personalized, precise, three-dimensional, and timely archive information services. Nowadays, due to the prominent problems of low efficiency and unsatisfactory recall accuracy in cross departmental and cross business archive retrieval in traditional archive management methods, this article proposes a "1+2N" (one standard and two extensions) distributed archive warehouse for co construction and sharing system architecture, which is based on the standard framework of the Smart Archive Repository Management Cloud Platform. The architecture uses scalable warehouses and modules to meet the personalized needs of archive management units of different sizes and requirements. The real-time dynamic update archive summary mechanism improves management efficiency, enhances information availability, and enhances security. The real-time transparent distributed archive retrieval mechanism meets users' demands for speed, accuracy, and scalability. The archive security access mechanism for privacy protection adopts technical means such as encryption, access control, backup and recovery, and audit monitoring to ensure the security of archive information. Through practical deployment and application, it has been shown that this architecture can effectively improve the management efficiency of distributed archives while ensuring archive security.

articleTitle: Comparison of LSTM and ARIMA Algorithms in Predicting Water Levels in Jakarta
abstract: This study evaluates the efficacy of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) algorithms in forecasting water levels (TMA) in Jakarta. The dataset encompasses water level measurements from multiple places in Jakarta from January to June 2024, consisting of 55,920 observations divided into 80% training data and 20% testing data using random sampling. Data preparation entails the use of normalization via MinMaxScaler for LSTM, but ARIMA requires stationarity testing and parameter selection guided by the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The investigation indicates that ARIMA marginally surpasses LSTM regarding Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), yielding values of 372.32 and 19.30, respectively. Simultaneously, LSTM has a reduced Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 13.82 in contrast to ARIMA’s 14.69. The LSTM’s Mean Squared Error (MSE) is 384.30, and the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) is 19.60. In conclusion, ARIMA is more adept at identifying data patterns related to MSE and RMSE, while LSTM is superior in minimizing average absolute error. The selection of the optimal model is contingent upon the prioritized evaluation metric and the dataset’s complexity.
